A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same DOT study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original DOT evaluations on mathematical reasoning and code generation, component ablations, training dynamics, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds general reasoning, open-ended and agentic evaluations, another model family, training-free comparisons, and training latency measurements.

M1.justification: The documented DOT procedure is unchanged: group-conditional outlier truncation, minimum truncation margin, reward recomputation, KL-Cov, and predictive dynamic sampling. Equations 4–6 and Algorithm 1 are retained. The new model and budget configurations do not introduce a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 extends evaluation beyond v1's math and code coverage to GPQA and MMLU, open-ended AlpacaEval 2.0 and ArenaHard, and agentic BFCL v3 tasks (Appendices D and F). The original training dataset and benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: New Table 9 adds training-free comparators TCC, CoD, NoThinking, Dynasor-CoT, SEAL, DEER, and DEER-Pro on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B. SEAL has results only for MATH-500; the others also have AIME-24 results. The comparator sets in Tables 1–4 are retained, and Table 11 adds a GRPO timing comparison.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Qwen3-4B with DOT-16K/32K configurations, length-controlled win rates, ArenaHard scoring, BFCL score and step metrics, and training latency measurements. These substantially extend the experimental settings and measurements. The original math evaluation protocol remains unchanged; detailed settings for the added experiments are only partially specified.

E4.justification: V2 adds targeted checks of model-family dependence and possible harm to agentic exploration, including BFCL step counts (Appendices E–F), plus a rollout/update timing breakdown (Appendix K). The original component ablations, threshold sensitivity tests, case studies, distribution analyses, and training curves are retained.

E5.justification: Both retain averaging over 32 generated outputs per math problem and the same variability displays. The new tables report point estimates without adding seed counts, repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their values, while Tables 5–9 and 11 add substantial results. Examples include GPQA accuracy/length of 35.39/9826 for Original versus 36.58/4791 for DOT-8K, and BFCL scores of 64.86, 63.89, and 64.98 for Original, DOT-16K, and DOT-32K. Table 11 newly reports average training-step times of 5m29s for GRPO and 3m39s for DOT-8K.

T1.justification: The GRPO formulation, truncation definitions, mathematical reasoning, and predictive sampling algorithm are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about length shift, selective outlier truncation, preserved exploration, and improved efficiency–performance trade-offs. The headline 78% token-reduction claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: New appendix interpretations argue that brevity transfers beyond math answer formats, is not specific to the DeepSeek family, preserves agentic decision structure, and reduces training idle time. These extend the existing interpretation. However, v2 retains the limitation stating that agentic tasks were not investigated, contradicting its new BFCL evaluation.

D1.justification: V2 adds model and code access links on the first page, plus detailed training durations, step counts, and rollout/update timings in Table 11. Existing hardware disclosures and the hyperparameter table remain unchanged. The new timings are additional disclosures, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for new benchmarks, training-free comparators, and background work, while removing the FuseO1 mention and its Wan et al. reference. Much of the expanded main-text related work already appeared in v1 Appendix I. The central positioning around RL-based efficient reasoning remains.

P1.justification: Compression and routing discussions move from Appendix I into Section 6, and the appendices are reorganized. V2 also adds author-role footnotes, acknowledgments, and an AI-assistant disclosure. Most existing scientific prose, including the method and core contributions, remains unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds six tables covering broader evaluations, Qwen3-4B, agentic score/steps, training-free comparisons, and detailed latency measurements. The DOT schematic moves from appendix Figure 9 to main-text Figure 4, with accompanying figure relocation and reflow. Existing graphical content and case-study displays are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens v1's math/code evidence with broader task and model evaluations, additional comparison methods, and measured training latency. These additions better support generality and practical efficiency, while code/model links improve access information. The gain is limited by sparse setup details for the new experiments and the retained statement that agentic tasks remain unexplored despite the new BFCL results.
